correctness.rationale: Original mathematical assertions check out: degree j Walsh characters have eigenvalue 2j and form a binomial-dimensional eigenspace, so PBH applies to coordinate-row restriction. For n=2k+1, incidence up/down commutation gives a direct harmonic decomposition. Substituting the lifts reduces the action to a function of t=|x∩R| for each ℓ-set R; repeated lowering and Newton expansion cancel all terms below order ℓ. The surviving difference gives (−2)^ℓ[z^(j−ℓ)](1−z²)^(k−ℓ)(1+z), which yields the stated nonzero signed binomial. Column complementation handles j>k. The original even product placement follows by taking row sums and differences over the last bit; an even middle shell has proportional antipodal rows in degree k. For the repaired spectrum claim, separately checked the commutator recurrence for the unnormalized iterated up-lifts F_r: D_r F_r=(r−ℓ)(n−r−ℓ+1)F_(r−1). This gives ||E_(r,ℓ)h||²=binom(n−2ℓ,r−ℓ)||h||² and orthogonality of distinct sectors by induction (D_r U_(r−1) is scalar on each source sector). Thus the singular values use the square root of the target/source norm factors, with sector dimensions binom(n,ℓ)−binom(n,ℓ−1), including the ℓ=0 case. The supplied integer and modular checks were inspected, not replayed; full rank mod the prime suffices for full real rank but is not a general upper-bound certificate for real rank. The original upper bound for the middle shell comes from exact row proportionality, not modular evidence; the repaired spectral normalization is proved rather than inferred from those tests.

value.rationale: For the known optimal odd sampling shell, recovering coefficients from node values benefits from knowing how each input mode is amplified, rather than merely knowing recoverability.
